text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Prime Minister Netanyahu clarifies: Oslo accords do not prevent continued settlement building.
- Treasury proposes to legislate salary raise for public sector officials.
- Lawmakers' salaries rose 3.4 percent, parliamentary committee to decide on additional 6.9 percent raise.
- Attorney General to inform High Court tomorrow if located state to shelter six Iraqis held in Israel.
- Palestinians fill only 70 percent of Israeli work permit quotas.
- 100 requests to boost exports ignored due to managerial problems.
- Bank of Israel bought 320 million shekels of foreign currency; internal discussion to widen band.
JERUSALEM POST
- Netanyahu says no to fully sovereign Palestinian state.
- Ma'aleh Ephraim settlement gets okay to expand.
- Palestinian President Arafat meets Hebron Islamic leaders, Hamas stays underground.
- Netanyahu to invite world's top CEO's to Israel.
- Court cancels tariffs on imported ice cream.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Plan to eject foreign workers and bring back workers from occupied territories.
- Israel to free 37 Palestinian female prisoners by start of February.
- Ministerial committee to discuss strengthening sovereignty in East Jerusalem.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu congratulates U.S. President Clinton: "together we'll reach peace and security."
- Unknown group threatens prime minister's life.
GLOBES
- Means of payment rose 2.2 percent in December, 12.3 percent rise in 1996.
- Estimates: 0.3 to 0.5 percent drop in interest rates, if at all.
